standard.title: Continuing Civil Rights Efforts in Australia
standard.description: the continuing efforts to create change in the civil rights and freedoms in Australia, for First Nations Australians, migrants and women
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have studied civil rights and freedoms in Australia to Year 9 level, including early campaigns for First Nations rights and women's rights.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify the continuing efforts to create change in the civil rights and freedoms of First Nations Australians, migrants and women, and examine Australia's international obligations including under UNDRIP.

nodes.label: Continuing civil rights action — First Nations Australians
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify areas that are the focus for continued civil rights action for First Nations Australians and discuss why the need for change continues.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two areas of ongoing civil rights action for First Nations Australians and explain why continued action is still needed.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and discuss why education, health care, housing, and employment remain areas of significant disadvantage and ongoing civil rights action for First Nations Australians; discuss the structural causes of ongoing inequality; connect to the gap between formal legal recognition (voting rights, land rights, Mabo) and substantive change in living conditions.
wider: Examine a specific current campaign by First Nations Australians — such as the calls for treaty, truth-telling, or addressing deaths in custody — tracing its historical roots in the events covered in K09–K11 and evaluating what progress has been made

Investigate Australia's obligations under UNDRIP in relation to a specific ongoing issue (e.g. land rights, cultural heritage protection), examining how the gap between international obligation and domestic policy operates

response_modes.reason: This node risks being taught as abstract statistics without connection to lived experience or historical cause. Ground the discussion in specific campaigns and connect each area of ongoing disadvantage to its historical cause in the legislation and policies examined in K09.

success_criteria: Identify at least two areas of ongoing civil rights action for First Nations Australians and explain why each remains an area of need
Connect at least one area of continuing disadvantage to a historical cause (legislation, policy) studied in K09–K11
Explain the gap between formal legal recognition and substantive change in living conditions for First Nations Australians

nodes.label: Continuing change — women and migrants
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can examine the continuing efforts to create change in the rights of women and migrants in Australia, and Australia's obligations under international human rights instruments.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least one area of continuing change in women's rights and one in migrants' rights since the late 20th century.
nodes.typical_width: Examine the changes in women's rights from suffrage through to contemporary protections — election to parliaments, employment law, reproductive rights, access to public places like hotels, protections against domestic and family violence; investigate changes in government policy on migrants (Racial Discrimination Act 1975) and how these policies have reflected and impacted Australia's changing place in the world; examine Australia's responsibilities as a signatory to UNDRIP (2007) and how it influences calls for recognising the rights of First Nations Australians and First Peoples in other countries.
wider: Investigate how Australia's obligations under multiple international human rights instruments (UNDRIP, CEDAW, ICCPR) interact with domestic policy, evaluating whether international pressure has driven or lagged behind domestic reform

Compare the civil rights trajectories of First Nations Australians, migrants and women since 1945, identifying where their campaigns intersected or diverged and evaluating which group has seen the most substantive change

response_modes.reason: This node integrates the three civil rights threads (First Nations, women, migrants) that have run through K07–K13, examining their continuing relevance alongside Australia's international obligations. It brings together the course's major social history themes.

success_criteria: Describe at least one area of continuing change in women's rights in Australia since the late 20th century
Explain how at least one piece of legislation or policy change since the 1970s has advanced migrants' rights in Australia
Explain Australia's obligations under UNDRIP (2007) and their significance for First Nations rights
